No DNS or Internet connection is needed. All used switch ports are access ports in VLAN 1. Use these public credentials only in the disposable lab:

| Purpose | Username or identifier | Lab value |
|---|---|---|
| Local recovery user | recovery | Lab-Recovery-2026! |
| Privileged EXEC secret | enable | Lab-Enable-2026! |
| Central user, absent locally | morgan | Lab-Morgan-2026! |
| TACACS+ device/server key | R1 client entry | Lab-Tacacs-Key-2026! |
| RADIUS device/server key | R1 client entry | Lab-Radius-Key-2026! |

steps.title: Cable and address the fresh devices
steps.body:
Create the listed models, use the exact table, and set PC/server IP values in Desktop → IP Configuration. Open the router through Admin-PC Terminal and keep that console available throughout. Decline the setup dialog if offered.

```ios R1
Router> enable
Router# configure terminal
Router(config)# hostname R1
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R1(config-if)# ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-if)# no shutdown
R1(config-if)# end
```

```ios SW1
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname SW1
SW1(config)# interface range fastethernet0/1 - 2
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport access vlan 1
SW1(config-if-range)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if-range)# exit
SW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 1
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# end
```

After forwarding begins, ping .1 and .100 from Admin-PC and ping .100 from R1.

:::expected
All intended local addresses are reachable and R1 Gi0/0 is up/up. These tests establish IP/ICMP reachability; the AAA service and accounts have not yet been tested.
:::

steps.title: Build and verify local SSH before AAA
steps.body:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# username recovery privilege 15 secret Lab-Recovery-2026!
R1(config)# enable secret Lab-Enable-2026!
R1(config)# ip domain-name lab.example
R1(config)# crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 2048
R1(config)# ip ssh version 2
R1(config)# line console 0
R1(config-line)# login local
R1(config-line)# exec-timeout 10 0
R1(config-line)# exit
R1(config)# line vty 0 4
R1(config-line)# login local
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# exec-timeout 5 0
R1(config-line)# end
R1# show running-config
R1# show ip ssh
```

If the RSA one-line form is unsupported, use `crypto key generate rsa` in global configuration and answer 2048 at its modulus prompt. Inspect the complete VTY configuration. If the image also has `line vty 5 15`, apply `login local`, `transport input ssh`, and `exec-timeout 5 0` to that existing range in line configuration mode too.

From Admin-PC Command Prompt run:

```text
ssh -l recovery 10.0.0.1
```

Enter the recovery password and run `show privilege`. Keep that tested SSH session open while exiting and reopening the console and verifying its local login. Return to privileged EXEC on the console, then close the SSH session with `exit`.

:::expected
Both fresh access paths authenticate recovery. `show privilege` reports 15. A legacy secret-storage type is a simulator limitation, not a modern password-storage recommendation. Record any unsupported SSH setup instead of proceeding to remote AAA with no tested recovery.
:::

steps.title: Enable explicit local AAA lists and save recovery
steps.body:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# aaa new-model
R1(config)# aaa authentication login default local
R1(config)# aaa authentication login CONSOLE local
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH local
R1(config)# line console 0
R1(config-line)# login authentication CONSOLE
R1(config-line)# exit
R1(config)# line vty 0 4
R1(config-line)# login authentication VTY-AUTH
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# end
```

If an additional VTY range was found, bind it to the same named list now:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# line vty 5 15
R1(config-line)# login authentication VTY-AUTH
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# end
```

Use the second block only for an existing range. Repeat a fresh recovery SSH login, keep it open while verifying a new console login again, and return to the console. Inspect the lists and line bindings in `show running-config`. Do not add EXEC or command authorization in this baseline.

Save R1 and SW1 with `copy running-config startup-config` and save the project as `aaa-local-baseline.pkt`. Use Save As `aaa-tacacs-work.pkt` before the next step.

:::expected
Both local-only lists work through their actual line bindings. Recovery remains available independently of the future central server. The separately saved baseline contains no remote-server dependency.
:::

steps.title: Configure the TACACS+ server and client
steps.body:
On AAA → Services → AAA, set Service On. Add a network client named R1 with Client IP `10.0.0.1`, Secret `Lab-Tacacs-Key-2026!`, and TACACS/TACACS+ server type as named by the GUI. Add central user `morgan` with password `Lab-Morgan-2026!`. Do not add `recovery` to the central service. Inspect the resulting client/user rows before configuring R1.

The following uses classic IOS server syntax, commonly available in simulator images:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# tacacs-server host 10.0.0.100 key Lab-Tacacs-Key-2026!
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group tacacs+ local
R1(config)# end
R1# show running-config
```

If the classic server command is rejected but named TACACS+ objects are available, use the complete TACACS+ translation in Step 12 and substitute group `MGMT-TAC` in this list. Do not configure both alternatives. If the image has no usable server-client syntax, keep the local baseline and perform the central tests as a paper exercise with the lesson's documented method results.

:::expected
The VTY list now selects the one defined TACACS+ server before local. The default and CONSOLE lists remain local-only. R1 is the server's client at .1; .50 is the SSH user endpoint and would be the wrong client IP for the AAA server entry.
:::

steps.title: Verify central success and an explicit rejection
steps.body:
Open a new SSH session as `morgan` and enter the central password. Inspect the resulting prompt and `show privilege` where allowed, then close the session. This lab configures login authentication only; do not require privilege 15 from the server. On a simple server that returns no privilege attributes, user EXEC is the expected starting point; the enable secret permits the deliberately configured lab elevation.

With the server On, attempt one Morgan login with a wrong password and one recovery login with its correct local password. Inspect server records or supported device evidence for a rejection. If the simulator handles unknown users differently, record it and use the explicit paper FAIL case; service reachability alone is not proof of the returned result.

:::expected
Morgan's intended authentication succeeds. An explicit central FAIL rejects the wrong password and stops the list. If the server explicitly rejects local-only recovery, R1 must not use local as a second chance. The console still uses CONSOLE local. A central ERROR would be a different case even if the service is reachable.
:::

steps.title: Observe TACACS+ service unavailability
steps.body:
Close remote test sessions. On AAA → Services → AAA, set Service Off. Start a fresh recovery SSH login. Then try Morgan, who does not exist locally. From the console inspect supported `show aaa servers` or `show tacacs` output; use Simulation to inspect the request path if available. A disabled TCP service might refuse a connection promptly or produce a timeout; do not require a fixed delay.

:::expected
When the TACACS+ group cannot complete authentication and returns ERROR, the local method can accept recovery. Morgan fails because the local database contains no Morgan account. A delay alone is not proof of this branch; correlate the controlled service state, selected list, and available evidence. Keep the service Off only for this step.
:::

steps.title: Restore TACACS+ service and save its working copy
steps.body:
Turn the AAA service On. Verify a new successful Morgan login and a new console recovery login while preserving a tested active session during the console check. Confirm `VTY-AUTH group tacacs+ local` or the chosen named-group equivalent and CONSOLE local. If a debug was used on supported software, stop it:

```ios R1
R1# undebug all
R1# show running-config
R1# copy running-config startup-config
```

Save as `aaa-tacacs-complete.pkt`. If remote policy must be rolled back, use the tested console and change only the VTY list to `aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH local`, test recovery SSH, and preserve the faulty evidence separately. Do not use `no aaa new-model` as a blind reset recipe.

:::expected
The service is restored and central authentication works. The working TACACS+ copy and independent local baseline remain saved. No debug is intentionally left running.
:::

steps.title: Open a clean copy for RADIUS and match its ports
steps.body:
Open `aaa-local-baseline.pkt`, then Save As `aaa-radius-work.pkt`. This avoids mixing two protocol exercises. Configure AAA → Services → AAA with Service On, client R1 at .1, RADIUS type, key `Lab-Radius-Key-2026!`, and central user Morgan with the table's password.

Inspect the server's displayed or documented RADIUS port. If configurable, select standard authentication 1812 and accounting 1813. If the simulator fixes the authentication port at 1645, use the explicit legacy pair 1645/1646 in the alternative below and record it. Do not assume every Packet Tracer release has the same GUI or port defaults. If no reliable port setting/evidence is available, use the standard pair as a paper configuration and do not claim a successful central test.

For a service at 1812/1813:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# radius-server host 10.0.0.100 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813 key Lab-Radius-Key-2026!
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group radius local
R1(config)# end
```

For the documented/observed legacy 1645 service, use this block instead:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# radius-server host 10.0.0.100 auth-port 1645 acct-port 1646 key Lab-Radius-Key-2026!
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group radius local
R1(config)# end
```

Choose exactly one. If the classic form is unsupported, use Step 12's named RADIUS block with the verified port pair and group `MGMT-RAD` instead. Accounting is not enabled merely by defining its destination port.

:::expected
R1's server address, client source, shared key, and selected authentication port match the service. VTY-AUTH uses RADIUS before local; CONSOLE remains local-only. The standard and legacy examples differ in explicit port values, not in fallback policy.
:::

steps.title: Verify RADIUS success and rejection
steps.body:
Repeat fresh Morgan authentication, then a wrong Morgan password. Test local-only recovery while central service is On and inspect the actual result. Use `show radius statistics` or `show aaa servers` where supported; otherwise use the controlled accounts, service configuration, and Simulation evidence with a stated limit. A direct `test aaa` command, if available, does not replace the SSH binding test.

:::expected
A valid central account can authenticate. An Access-Reject is a completed denial and does not allow local fallback. An Access-Challenge continues authentication rather than meaning either success or server failure. No per-command authorization or accounting outcome is asserted by these login-only tests.
:::

steps.title: Observe RADIUS unavailability
steps.body:
Set the AAA service Off, close prior test sessions, and attempt a new recovery login. Try the central-only Morgan account separately. Observe the supported request/timeout evidence from the console or Simulation.

:::expected
An unavailable RADIUS method can return ERROR and advance to local, where recovery succeeds and Morgan fails. Retries, dead-server state, and timers affect timing; do not require a five-second pause or infer the selected method from delay alone.
:::

steps.title: Restore RADIUS and save its working copy
steps.body:
Turn the service On, verify a new Morgan session, and confirm the console recovery path. Stop any optional debug, inspect the selected list and complete VTY bindings, and save R1 with `copy running-config startup-config`. Save the project as `aaa-radius-complete.pkt`.

:::expected
RADIUS service is restored, its configured authentication port is documented, and the final copy has no induced outage. The TACACS+ complete copy and local baseline remain separate. An unsuccessful simulator branch is recorded as incomplete execution, not passed from paper expectations alone.
:::

steps.title: Translate both clients to named server objects
steps.body:
Complete this worksheet using the same addresses/keys. On an appropriate IOS/IOS XE lab image you may apply it to a fresh copy of the local baseline. It is not an additional block to paste over the already configured legacy server definitions.

```ios R1 TACACS+ alternative
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# tacacs server TAC1
R1(config-server-tacacs)# address ipv4 10.0.0.100
R1(config-server-tacacs)# key Lab-Tacacs-Key-2026!
R1(config-server-tacacs)# exit
R1(config)# aaa group server tacacs+ MGMT-TAC
R1(config-sg-tacacs+)# server name TAC1
R1(config-sg-tacacs+)# exit
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local
R1(config)# end
```

```ios R1 RADIUS alternative
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# radius server RAD1
R1(config-radius-server)# address ipv4 10.0.0.100 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813
R1(config-radius-server)# key Lab-Radius-Key-2026!
R1(config-radius-server)# exit
R1(config)# aaa group server radius MGMT-RAD
R1(config-sg-radius)# server name RAD1
R1(config-sg-radius)# exit
R1(config)# aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-RAD local
R1(config)# end
```

The RADIUS translation must use the server's actual selected pair; replace 1812/1813 with 1645/1646 only if that is the verified service. Identify the server object, group, method list, and already existing VTY binding in each translation.

:::expected
TAC1 belongs to MGMT-TAC; RAD1 belongs to MGMT-RAD. The existing `login authentication VTY-AUTH` line binding selects whichever explicitly configured method list the chosen copy uses. CONSOLE is unaffected. Named configuration changes the organization of the client definition; it does not by itself enable server features or prove access.
:::

lab.troubleshooting:
- New SSH session fails before authentication → check LAN reachability, SSH keys/status, VTY transport and restrictions before diagnosing a password.
- Central FAIL → inspect account and policy; local is not a rejection override.
- Group ERROR → inspect address, source/client entry, key, transport port, path, and service; a ping proves none of the AAA-specific settings.
- No central requests during a fresh login → inspect the selected list and binding; do not infer method selection only from login speed.
- Authentication succeeds but shell fails on an extended setup → inspect EXEC authorization independently and apply only the approved fallback policy.
- If remote access is lost, use tested CONSOLE local and restore VTY-AUTH local. If that recovery was not verified, return to the separately saved baseline rather than guessing through a live management change.
lab.challenge:
A new routed management design requires R1 to source TACACS+ from Loopback0 at 10.255.0.1/32. The server still has only a client definition for 10.0.0.1. Its routing table also lacks a route to 10.255.0.1. Identify the two independent corrections beyond creating/addressing Loopback0 and selecting it as the supported TACACS+ source interface. Explain why changing the user's password does not address either problem. This is a paper extension; do not alter the working flat lab.

:::expected
The server must recognize 10.255.0.1 as the permitted AAA client with the intended shared key, and the network must provide a valid return route to that source address. Any path controls must also permit the selected protocol. The user password belongs to the separate user-authentication decision; it does not define NAS source identity or routing. After those changes, test a fresh correctly bound management login and rejection/outage behavior while preserving CONSOLE local.
:::

questions.prompt: A valid SSH login succeeds, but the server denies configure terminal through a command policy. Which AAA function made that denial?
options: Authorization.
Authentication.
Session accounting.
IP route selection.
questions.explanation: Authentication accepted the identity claim. Authorization decides permitted actions; accounting can record the result without being the permission decision.

whyWrong.1: The identity check already succeeded.
whyWrong.2: Recording an event is not the command-permission decision.
whyWrong.3: Route selection is not an AAA policy function.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default
 transport input ssh
No username entries

questions.prompt: No local usernames exist in the complete relevant configuration. Why do these VTY logins fail?
options: A central server group is mandatory even for local-only AAA.
The selected local method has no account with which to authenticate the user.
The presence of AAA automatically disables the SSH transport.
The line password is sufficient but the domain suffix is wrong.
questions.explanation: The explicit selected list is local, so valid local account data is required. AAA can operate without a central server; enabling its framework is not a substitute for creating accounts.

whyWrong.0: Local-only authentication is a valid explicit design.
whyWrong.2: Transport input ssh remains a separate setting.
whyWrong.3: This list does not select the line-password method, and no DNS dependency is shown.

questions.prompt: Which conventional transport and service port does TACACS+ use?
options: TCP 22.
TCP 49.
questions.explanation: TACACS+ carries its separate AAA exchanges over TCP port 49. SSH to the router is a different client/server relationship.

whyWrong.0: UDP 1813 is conventional RADIUS accounting.
whyWrong.1: TCP 22 is SSH rather than the router-to-TACACS+ exchange.
whyWrong.3: UDP 1812 is conventional RADIUS authentication.

questions.prompt: Which two statements correctly describe conventional RADIUS/UDP? Select two.
options: An Access-Accept can carry authorization attributes with its successful result.
Its ordinary User-Password protection encrypts the entire IP packet.
It uses the TACACS+ TCP-49 per-command authorization exchange.
Authentication normally uses UDP 1812 and accounting UDP 1813.
questions.explanation: Conventional RADIUS combines the successful access decision with associated attributes, while accounting has separate messages/port. The ordinary password-hiding comparison does not mean whole-packet encryption.

whyWrong.1: The conventional User-Password hiding mechanism does not protect the entire packet.
whyWrong.2: RADIUS is not the TACACS+ command protocol.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local
Selected list: VTY-AUTH
Current central result: FAIL

questions.prompt: The central method returns an explicit authentication FAIL. What does this login list do?
options: Reject this attempt without trying the local method.
Try the local password because every first-method failure means fallback.
Accept the enable secret even though enable is not a listed method.
Bypass authentication because the server was reachable.
questions.explanation: FAIL is a completed denial and stops authentication. ERROR is the result that can advance to the next method; reachability is not itself permission.

whyWrong.1: A rejection is different from a method that cannot complete its decision.
whyWrong.2: The enable method is not part of this list.
whyWrong.3: A reachable service can explicitly deny access.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
Selected: VTY-AUTH = group MGMT-TAC local
Group result: ERROR
Local recovery account exists and credentials are valid

questions.prompt: All eligible group methods return ERROR and the supplied recovery credentials match a local account. What happens next?
options: The console list replaces VTY-AUTH automatically.
The next local method can authenticate the recovery account.
An ERROR is always an explicit credential rejection, so the attempt must stop there.
AAA grants access without checking any remaining method.
questions.explanation: ERROR permits advancement to the next method. Local still must accept valid account credentials; the line does not inherit the console list and does not become unauthenticated.

whyWrong.0: A console binding does not automatically replace a VTY binding.
whyWrong.2: FAIL is the explicit-denial branch; ERROR means this method could not complete authentication.
whyWrong.3: The remaining local method still makes a real check.

questions.prompt: Which line-configuration command binds the named login list VTY-AUTH?
options: aaa authentication VTY-AUTH
accounting exec VTY-AUTH
login authentication VTY-AUTH
authorization exec VTY-AUTH
questions.explanation: The login authentication line command selects a login list. Authorization and accounting are separate list types and do not bind login authentication.

whyWrong.0: AAA list definition commands belong to global configuration and use different syntax.
whyWrong.1: This selects accounting rather than the login check.
whyWrong.3: This selects an EXEC authorization list, not login authentication.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
VTY-AUTH = group MGMT-TAC local
Before fresh attempt: requests 10, timeouts 2
After: requests 11, timeouts 3
Observed method result: ERROR; local recovery accepted

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is supported by the current controlled test?
options: The central service rejected the user and that rejection authorized local fallback.
No central requests were sent because the counter increased only historically.
The device has proved the exact fault is a wrong user password.
The selected central method could not complete the exchange, allowing its configured local fallback.
questions.explanation: The test correlates new requests and timeouts with the selected method’s ERROR and local success. Investigate service/path/client/key settings; these counters do not identify one unique cause.

whyWrong.0: An explicit rejection would stop this authentication list.
whyWrong.1: The exhibit provides a before/after change for this fresh attempt.
whyWrong.2: A timeout does not prove an incorrect user secret.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text: radius-server host 10.0.0.100 auth-port 1645 acct-port 1646 key [omitted]

questions.prompt: Which listening ports must the server match for the shown classic RADIUS client definition?
options: UDP 1645 for authentication and UDP 1646 for accounting.
UDP 1812 for authentication and UDP 1813 for accounting.
TCP 49 for both authentication and accounting.
TCP 22 for authentication and UDP 1646 for accounting.
questions.explanation: The explicitly configured port keywords select the legacy pair. Do not infer standard ports from the RADIUS name or rely on an image default when the configuration gives the values.

whyWrong.1: Those are the standard pair but not the shown explicit values.
whyWrong.2: TCP 49 is TACACS+, not this RADIUS definition.
whyWrong.3: SSH is a different management transport.

questions.prompt: Which two statements explain the documented classic TACACS+ device-administration model accurately? Select two.
options: Its cleartext header means no shared key is needed.
It has separate authorization exchanges that support command policy.
Its body obfuscation is not a substitute for a protected management path.
Its UDP transport is what supplies per-command authorization.
questions.explanation: Separate exchanges support TACACS+ command control on relevant IOS configurations. RFC 8907 calls the classic body mechanism obfuscation and requires a secure deployment; do not equate it with modern authenticated transport encryption.

whyWrong.0: A shared key is still required for the documented protected client/server exchange.
whyWrong.3: TACACS+ uses TCP, and the command policy comes from its protocol/application model.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local
aaa authorization exec default group MGMT-TAC
Server method returns ERROR; local login succeeds; EXEC authorization fails.
Local recovery account has the approved privilege.

questions.prompt: The approved outage policy allows defined local accounts with their local privilege levels. Which correction meets that policy?
options: Enable console authorization to make the remote server reachable.
Remove local from login authentication so authorization no longer matters.
Add local as the fallback to the EXEC authorization list.
Add if-authenticated and treat it as exactly the same local-account check.
questions.explanation: Authentication and EXEC authorization have separate method lists. A local EXEC fallback can enforce the stated local-account policy after central ERROR; if-authenticated is a different, broader decision and is not interchangeable.

whyWrong.0: Console authorization does not fix server reachability.
whyWrong.1: Removing recovery authentication does not meet the required outage access policy.
whyWrong.3: It does not perform the same local-user authorization policy check.

questions.prompt: Which role can an appropriately deployed Cisco ISE service perform in this management design?
options: The SSH client on the administrator’s laptop, replacing the router’s server definition.
A mandatory process inside every IOS router’s local username database.
A forwarding next hop required for each user data packet after login.
A central AAA server using TACACS+ for device administration and RADIUS for supported access services.
questions.explanation: ISE provides central identity/policy services, including the relevant protocol capabilities when deployed and licensed appropriately. The router is its AAA client; this does not place ISE in every data forwarding path.

whyWrong.0: The administrator’s SSH client and central AAA service are different roles.
whyWrong.1: ISE is a separate service, not the router’s local username database.
whyWrong.2: AAA authentication does not make ISE a mandatory transit router.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
aaa authentication login CONSOLE local
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local
line con 0
 login authentication CONSOLE
line vty 0 4
 login authentication VTY-AUTH

questions.prompt: While the central group returns ERROR, which access behavior follows from these explicit bindings?
options: Console uses local immediately; VTY can reach local after the central method cannot complete.
Console waits on MGMT-TAC; VTY ignores its bound list and uses CONSOLE.
Both paths allow access without validating credentials.
Both paths require a central PASS before any local check.
questions.explanation: The console is explicitly bound to a local-only list. VTY-AUTH contains a central group followed by local, so the ERROR branch can select local there; both still require accepted credentials.

whyWrong.1: The named bindings specify the opposite relationship.
whyWrong.2: Local is an authentication method, not no authentication.
whyWrong.3: The VTY list expressly includes the local ERROR fallback, and console has no central method.

questions.prompt: Which command requests records at EXEC session start and stop on supporting IOS?
options: aaa authentication login default group MGMT-TAC local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group MGMT-TAC
aaa accounting exec default stop-only group MGMT-TAC
aaa authorization exec default group MGMT-TAC local
questions.explanation: EXEC start-stop accounting requests session lifecycle records. Verify delivery at the server; this does not automatically record every command.

whyWrong.0: Login authentication checks identity rather than recording the session lifecycle.
whyWrong.2: Stop-only requests a stop record rather than both lifecycle points.
whyWrong.3: Authorization decides permitted shell access, not the requested accounting events.

exhibit.title: Representative teaching evidence
exhibit.text:
Admin-PC SSH source: 10.0.0.50
R1 configured AAA source: Loopback0 10.255.0.1
AAA server: 10.0.0.100
Routing to/from Loopback0 is verified.

questions.prompt: Which server-side client address must be recognized for these management AAA requests?
options: 10.0.0.100, because it receives the AAA request.
Any address in the client LAN, because a shared key replaces source identity.
10.255.0.1, the selected and reachable NAS source.
10.0.0.50, because it initiates the SSH connection.
questions.explanation: The AAA service recognizes the NAS/router request source. The source also needs return reachability and matching client/key policy; the SSH user’s address is a different endpoint.

whyWrong.0: That is the server’s own address.
whyWrong.1: A matching shared key does not justify arbitrary unregistered client sources.
whyWrong.3: That is the SSH client address, not this AAA request source.

questions.prompt: Which configuration pair must share the same device/server key?
options: Morgan’s login password and R1’s enable secret.
Admin-PC’s hostname and R1’s domain suffix.
The server’s default gateway and the router’s local username.
R1’s AAA server definition and the server’s client entry for R1.
questions.explanation: The shared key belongs to the NAS-to-server relationship. User credentials and enable access are separate decisions; forcing them to equal the shared key would conflate independent secrets.

whyWrong.0: User authentication and enable access do not define the client/server shared key.
whyWrong.1: Hostnames/suffixes are not the shared secret pair.
whyWrong.2: Gateway addresses and usernames are different configuration fields.

cards.front: What are authentication, authorization, and accounting?
cards.back: Identity verification, permission decisions, and selected activity records. Success in one function does not establish success in the others.

cards.front: What conventional transport/port does TACACS+ use?
cards.back: TCP 49 for its separate authentication, authorization, and accounting exchanges.

cards.front: What are conventional RADIUS ports and the legacy pair?
cards.back: UDP 1812 authentication/authorization and 1813 accounting; legacy 1645/1646 exists. Explicitly match the service rather than assume platform defaults.

cards.front: How do classic TACACS+ and RADIUS protection scopes compare?
cards.back: TACACS+ obscures the body, not header; RFC 8907 calls it obfuscation. Conventional RADIUS hides User-Password, not the whole packet. Protect the management path; extensions can differ.

cards.front: Where can RADIUS provide authorization attributes?
cards.back: In the Access-Accept associated with successful access authentication. Accounting uses separate messages. This differs from TACACS+ separate authorization exchanges.

cards.front: Which model supplies TACACS+-style per-command authorization?
cards.back: TACACS+ on supporting device configurations. Configure the intended privilege/context coverage; an EXEC login alone does not enable every command check.

cards.front: What are common TACACS+ and RADIUS uses?
cards.back: TACACS+ for device administration; RADIUS for network access and also supported management authentication. Typical use is not an exclusivity rule.

cards.front: How are these protocols documented?
cards.back: TACACS+ has Cisco origins and RFC 8907 is Informational. RADIUS authentication/accounting is specified in RFC 2865/2866. Origin does not establish modern protection strength.

cards.front: What role can Cisco ISE serve?
cards.back: A central AAA/policy service with RADIUS and TACACS+ capabilities under the appropriate deployment/licensing. The managed router remains the AAA client.

cards.front: Who is the AAA client during an administrator’s SSH login?
cards.back: The router/NAS is the AAA client of the central service, while it is the SSH server for the administrator. The two source identities differ.

cards.front: What should accompany enabling aaa new-model?
cards.back: A precreated recovery account, tested SSH and console, explicit lists/bindings, and a saved baseline. Verify fresh sessions instead of relying on implicit line behavior.

cards.front: When does a login method list advance to the next method?
cards.back: On ERROR, when the method cannot complete authentication. Explicit FAIL denies the attempt. ERROR can include more than an offline server.

cards.front: How do you define a central-first named VTY list with local fallback?
cards.back: aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local. Local is a fallback for method ERROR, not a second password chance after rejection.

cards.front: How is a named login list bound to a VTY line?
cards.back: In that line’s configuration: login authentication VTY-AUTH. Inspect and configure every existing VTY range intentionally.

cards.front: What defines a modern named TACACS+ or RADIUS server?
cards.back: tacacs server NAME or radius server NAME, then address ipv4 and key in its submode. Specify RADIUS auth-port/acct-port to match the service.

cards.front: How can classic IOS define a RADIUS service explicitly?
cards.back: radius-server host 10.0.0.100 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813 key KEY. Use the actual supported port pair; do not rely on legacy defaults.

cards.front: How is a named server added to its protocol group?
cards.back: aaa group server tacacs+ MGMT-TAC, then server name TAC1; use the radius group type for a named RADIUS definition.

cards.front: What do EXEC start-stop and stop-only accounting request?
cards.back: Session start and stop records, or only the stop record. They do not automatically record each command; verify collection and failure behavior.

cards.front: How should AAA verification combine tests and evidence?
cards.back: Inspect line→list→group→server configuration, correlate a fresh login with supported counters/server records, and test rejection/outage separately. A direct test aaa result does not prove VTY binding.

cards.front: Does a five-second login delay prove AAA failure or console behavior?
cards.back: No. Timers, retries, group state, and other operations vary. Inspect actual method results; console authentication and console authorization are separate deliberate settings.

commands.task: Enable the AAA framework after creating and testing the local recovery path.
commands.note: Immediately follow with deliberate lists and line bindings; do not rely on undocumented defaults.

commands.task: Enter a modern TACACS+ server definition named TAC1.
commands.note: Configure its reachable address and shared key in the server submode.

commands.task: Set this TACACS+ definition’s server address to 10.0.0.100.
commands.note: The AAA server must recognize the NAS source and matching shared key.

commands.task: Set this RADIUS server to 10.0.0.100 with standard authentication and accounting UDP ports explicitly.
commands.note: The actual service must listen on the same ports; defining accounting’s port does not enable accounting.

commands.task: Create the named TACACS+ group MGMT-TAC.
commands.note: Add the intended named server definitions to this protocol group.

commands.task: Add the already-defined TAC1 server to this TACACS+ group.
commands.note: The referenced definition must exist; a group name is distinct from a login-list name.

commands.task: Make VTY-AUTH try MGMT-TAC first and local only after method ERROR.
commands.answer: aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local
commands.note: An explicit central rejection stops authentication and does not invoke local.

commands.task: Create a local-only login list named CONSOLE.
commands.note: Bind it deliberately to line console 0 and verify a fresh console login.

commands.task: Bind this console line to the named CONSOLE login list.
commands.note: This is login authentication, not EXEC authorization or a password-free exception.

commands.task: Set the default EXEC authorization list to group MGMT-TAC, then local as the approved outage fallback.
commands.answer: aaa authorization exec default group MGMT-TAC local
commands.note: if-authenticated is not an equivalent local-user policy check. Test remote authorization without extending it to the console blindly.

commands.task: Define the default EXEC accounting list to request start/stop records through MGMT-TAC.
commands.answer: aaa accounting exec default start-stop group MGMT-TAC
commands.note: Verify actual server receipt; this is session accounting rather than automatic per-command accounting.

commands.task: On a CML IOL image supporting the documented legacy test form, test TACACS+ group MGMT-TAC with user morgan and disposable password Lab-Morgan-2026!.
commands.answer: test aaa group MGMT-TAC morgan Lab-Morgan-2026! legacy
commands.note: Cisco documents this named TACACS+ test on CML IOL. Some IOS references restrict test aaa to RADIUS; do not assume Packet Tracer support. It tests the group, not VTY binding; use fresh SSH and server evidence when unavailable.

tickets.title: An explicit local AAA list has no accounts
tickets.scenario: BR1 is reachable by SSH and a privileged console session remains open. A change selected local AAA for the VTY lines, but the complete relevant configuration contains no local username. These are representative records.

exhibits.title: Current authentication
exhibits.text:
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default
 transport input ssh
No username entries

exhibits.title: Observed test
exhibits.text: Fresh SSH reaches authentication and no submitted local account is accepted.

tickets.question: Which missing dependency explains the selected method’s failure?
options: A TACACS+ server is mandatory for any AAA login.
The local database contains no valid account for the selected local method.
SSH transport cannot coexist with AAA new-model.
The router must remove its enable secret before using local authentication.
tickets.explanation: The list explicitly selects local and there is no local identity to validate. Correct that dependency from the retained authorized console, then test fresh sessions and a separate console recovery list. No implicit-default assumption or central server is needed for this diagnosis.
tickets.fix:
In the disposable lab, from the retained privileged console:
```ios
BR1# configure terminal
BR1(config)# username recovery privilege 15 secret Lab-Recovery-2026!
BR1(config)# aaa authentication login CONSOLE local
BR1(config)# line console 0
BR1(config-line)# login authentication CONSOLE
BR1(config-line)# end
```
Test a fresh recovery SSH login. Keep it open while verifying a fresh console login, then inspect every VTY range and save the intended configuration. Replace public examples with approved unique secrets outside a disposable lab.

tickets.title: The central list exists but the VTY uses local
tickets.scenario: R2 has one TACACS+ server TAC1 in MGMT-TAC. A controlled new SSH login uses a local account instantly. The central service sees no request and the device’s request counter does not increase. The complete VTY configuration for this test is shown.

exhibits.title: Definitions and methods
exhibits.text:
tacacs server TAC1
 address ipv4 10.0.0.100
 key [omitted]
aaa group server tacacs+ MGMT-TAC
 server name TAC1
aaa authentication login default local
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local

exhibits.title: Actual selected VTY configuration
exhibits.text:
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default
 transport input ssh

exhibits.title: Fresh-attempt counter comparison
exhibits.text: TACACS+ authentication requests before: 0; after: 0

tickets.question: Which configuration change selects the intended central-first login policy?
options: Bind login authentication VTY-AUTH to the intended VTY range.
Change the central user password because no request reached the service.
Replace the router’s reachable server address without testing it.
Use the SSH client IP as the server’s NAS client address.
tickets.explanation: The VTY explicitly selects default, which is local-only. The unbound VTY-AUTH list therefore does not participate. The current binding plus unchanged request counter supports this diagnosis; instant timing alone would not.
tickets.fix:
Keep the tested local console session open:
```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# line vty 0 4
R2(config-line)# login authentication VTY-AUTH
R2(config-line)# end
```
Apply the intended binding to any additional existing VTY ranges. Test a fresh central success, explicit rejection, and controlled ERROR fallback while keeping console recovery. Save only after those results match policy.

sections.title: Names, sequence numbers and safe edits

lab.title: Build and verify an IPv4 access policy in both directions
lab.intro:
Use a new Packet Tracer file and devices with default configurations. You will establish connectivity before filtering, compare standard and extended lists, insert an exception, restrict management, and diagnose a missing return rule. Work through R1's local CLI tab so a management restriction cannot disconnect your configuration session.

All output below is representative teaching evidence, not a capture from an executed simulator. Exact port aliases, counters and failure messages vary. If output filters such as `| section` are unavailable, read the full running configuration. Sequence editing and resequencing vary by image; a complete replacement-list fallback is provided. The finished lab demonstrates a limited policy, not a stateful firewall.

Return traffic enters the opposite interface.", "nodes": [ { "id": "A", "kind": "pc", "label": "PC-A", "sub": "10.100.10.10", "x": 1, "y": 1 }, { "id": "B", "kind": "pc", "label": "PC-B", "sub": "10.100.10.11", "x": 1, "y": 5 }, { "id": "S1", "kind": "switch", "label": "SW1", "x": 3, "y": 3 }, { "id": "R", "kind": "router", "label": "R1", "sub": ".1 in each /24", "x": 6, "y": 3 }, { "id": "S2", "kind": "switch", "label": "SW2", "x": 9, "y": 3 }, { "id": "W", "kind": "server", "label": "WEB", "sub": "10.100.20.20", "x": 11, "y": 1 }, { "id": "F", "kind": "server", "label": "FILES", "sub": "10.100.20.30", "x": 11, "y": 5 } ], "links": [ { "from": "A", "to": "S1", "toLabel": "Fa0/1" }, { "from": "B", "to": "S1", "toLabel": "Fa0/2" }, { "from": "S1", "to": "R", "fromLabel": "Gi0/1", "toLabel": "G0/0" }, { "from": "R", "to": "S2", "fromLabel": "G0/1", "toLabel": "Gi0/1" }, { "from": "S2", "to": "W", "fromLabel": "Fa0/1" }, { "from": "S2", "to": "F", "fromLabel": "Fa0/2" } ] }
